channel.title: Fintech — Nicholas Garcia
channel.description: Payment rails, bank–fintech partnerships, stablecoins and licensing, and who carries the risk.

item.title: When an Embedded-Finance Middleman Fails, Who Answers for the Money?
item.description: Synapse's April 2024 bankruptcy left a shortfall of $60 million to $90 million between partner-bank records and its own, and customers waited weeks or months for their funds.

item.title: An MAS Licence Covers Singapore Only
item.description: A licence under Singapore's Payment Services Act settles whether a firm may offer payment services in Singapore; Jakarta, Bangkok and Manila each decide that for themselves.

item.title: What Backs a Stablecoin When Its Bank Fails
item.description: When SVB failed in March 2023, about $3.3 billion of USDC reserves, roughly 8 percent of the total, sat at the failed bank.

item.title: Sponsor Banks Keep the Compliance Risk for Their Fintech Partners
item.description: US interagency guidance from June 2023 and a July 2024 joint statement say the bank keeps the compliance liability, whoever owns the app.

item.title: Instant Payments Leave No Time to Stop Fraud
item.description: Since October 2024, UK payment firms must refund Faster Payments scam victims up to £85,000 per claim; in the US, Zelle victims bore more than 80 percent of 2023 scam losses.
